title: Trenches and Total War Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll head to the Western Front — and trace how WWI was fought, lost and won.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Schlieffen Plan, trench warfare, Somme, Verdun and the end of WWI.

concepts.def: Germany's 1914 plan to defeat France in 6 weeks
Sept 1914 battle that halted the German advance
Stalemate of dug-in armies along a 400-mile front
1916 British offensive — 57,000 casualties on day one

walkthroughs.body_html:
Germany planned to beat France in 6 weeks by sweeping through Belgium.

It nearly worked. But Belgian resistance, the British Expeditionary Force and the French at the Marne stopped them in September 1914. Both sides dug trenches — stalemate began.

The Western Front stretched around 400 miles from the Channel to Switzerland.

Soldiers faced mud, lice, rats, shellfire and gas. Verdun in 1916 lasted ten months. The Somme began on 1 July 1916 — Britain lost about 57,000 casualties on the first day alone.

The USA joined the war in April 1917. Russia left after revolution in 1917.

Germany's Spring Offensive in 1918 failed. The Allied 'Hundred Days' pushed them back. Mutiny and revolution broke out at home. The Armistice was signed at 11am on 11 November 1918.
